neighbours.label: A hedging or concessive connective right after an evaluative remark ('fascinating, if you ask me', 'lovely, if a little X', 'a marvel on its own'), vs ordinary conditional 'if'
fire: The new bridge is a beautiful piece of design, if you ask me.
Her latest novel is charming, if a bit too long in the middle.
That old diner makes the best pancakes in town, if you ask me.
The waterfall is an impressive sight on its own, but the canyon is better.
The lecture was entertaining, if not especially deep.
The little robot is great fun, if rather pointless.
The remastered album sounds wonderful, if you ask me.
His painting was a delight on its own, even without the frame.
quiet: The new bridge will open to traffic if the inspection is passed.
Her latest novel will be translated if the sales stay strong.
That old diner closes early if it rains on a weekday.
The waterfall can be reached on foot, but the trail is steep.
The lecture will be recorded if enough students sign up.
The little robot stops moving if its battery runs low.
Ask the clerk if the album is still in stock.
His painting was sold at auction, along with the frame.

predictions: Evaluative remark + if/on/in fact 0.2-0.6; conditional if and sentence-initial 'If you ask me' under 0.05.
notes: Card: 'Fascinating stuff, if you ask me', 'Very fun, if useless', 'so good, in fact', 'sight on its own'. Probe: 'marvel on its own' 0.583, 'stunning, if you ask me' 0.504, 'clever, if somewhat useless' 0.389, 'so good, in fact' 0.278, 'lovely, if a little' 0.188; initial 'If you ask me' 0.035, 'Call me if' 0.016, 'only if' 0.003.
